title: Perfect pitch and classmate Henry Coker
summary: Gus has near-perfect pitch; Henry Coker, with his father's beat-up trombone, was in his music class.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I was doing Jonah not so long ago, and Jonah would sing about Stuff, that Stuff would call -- the this bus would blow the horn and stuff and he'd tell you, C-sharp and anything, everything he would hear, every time he'd call it.
Like Henry Coker, the trombone plaver?
Oh, yeah, yeah?
Well, he and I were in the same music class.
Oh, is that right? Is that right?
Right.
Fancy that. Well, he was playing in
the band.
Oh, yeah, sure.
He had his horn.
And he had his horn.
I suppose he had just been given a trombone?
He had this beat-up Trombone that was his daddy's.
Oh, is that right?
And he was long and lanky, I was long and lanky.
Oh, you started to shoot up by then, right?
Oh, yes. I was skinny, I was just skinny, but he was always taller than I was at the time.
Oh, was he? Yeah.
And I had grown then, see.
Yeah.
Because in Houston, I was short.
Yeah.
Like I said, when --
When you hit your 14, you began to --
Yeah, I was working in the drugstore and all like that, and riding the bicycle out. I started growing like that.
Yeah.
And I came to Dallas, I still had me a little job, working at the drugstore.
Yeah, yeah. Well, you needed to -- for some change, so you could have some fun.
Oh, yeah.
